_comment: Fixed inference workload for reranker latency benchmark. Scaled down from original (10q×20docs×500tok) to (5q×20docs×200tok) so 3 cells × 5 iterations finishes in ~3 min. Varied lengths still stress dynamic padding.
queries: How does the reranker normalise raw logits to a zero-to-one score?
Which ONNX execution provider does the reranker prefer on Apple Silicon?
Why was CoreML disabled by default for the cross-encoder model?
What batch size does the reranker use for inference?
What happens when the reranker model fails to load at runtime?
seed_texts: The cross-encoder reranker takes a query and a candidate document as a single input pair, tokenises them together, and produces a single relevance logit. This logit is passed through a sigmoid function to normalise the score into the zero-to-one range, making it comparable with vector cosine similarity scores returned by the dense retrieval stage.

Reranker threshold scaling divides the raw cross-encoder logit by a factor of thirty before applying the sigmoid transformation. This empirical calibration was derived from a threshold-calibration experiment that measured the score distribution across relevant and non-relevant query-document pairs.

On Apple Silicon Macs the reranker attempts to use the CoreML execution provider to push inference onto the Apple Neural Engine, falling back to the CPU execution provider if CoreML is unavailable or rejects the graph. The provider list is ordered by preference.
